title: Peach Tarte Tatin with Amber Glaze
changes_from_base: Peaches in place of apples; the caramel starts from butter and sugar in the pan, and the fruit juice is drained after baking and boiled into a brushed glaze.
summary: The classic upside-down Tatin made with peaches, with their pan juices boiled down into a dark glaze brushed on at the end.
equipment: 23 cm ovenproof heavy frying pan or Tatin tin

ingredients.item: ripe but firm peaches (about 7), peeled, stoned and quartered
fine sea salt or table salt
plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: rub or pulse the flour, icing sugar, salt and diced butter to fine crumbs. Mix the yolk with the iced water, stir it in until the dough clumps, then flatten into a disc, wrap and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: roll the dough on baking paper to a 25 cm round, fold the edge under to make a 23 cm round with a slight rim, cut 3 short slits in the middle and chill on the sheet. Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).

steps.title: Pan
steps.text: spread the soft butter over the base of the pan, scatter the 100 g sugar evenly on top and sprinkle with the salt. Pack the peach quarters in a ring around the edge, then squeeze the rest into the centre.

steps.title: Caramelise
steps.text: cook over high heat, without stirring, for 8-12 min, until the pink juice turns deep amber. Move the pan around the burner if one side browns faster. Peaches give off more juice than apples, so the colour change is your guide, not the clock.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: off the heat, lay the pastry on top so it sits inside the rim. Brush it with water, scatter over the crust sugar and bake 30-35 min, until the crust is a rich brown. Cool on the rack for 20 min.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: put the plate on the crust, hold it firmly and tip the pan over the heatproof bowl so the juice runs out. Set the pan back down and give it a shake to settle the fruit, then turn the tart out onto the plate.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: pour the juice back into the hot pan and boil hard, stirring, for 2-3 min until dark and syrupy. Cool 2-3 min until it is like runny honey, brush it over the peaches and leave 20 min before slicing. Watch closely; it goes from dark to burnt in seconds.

tips: Pick peaches that give only slightly when pressed; soft ones collapse in the pan.
To peel peaches easily, dip them in boiling water for 30 s, then into iced water.
Draining the juice keeps the crust crisp under the fruit.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Cover and keep at room temperature for up to 1 day; warm slices in a 160 °C oven for 10 min.
